 Judgment

This is a Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.40,00,000/ for the Death of one Banda Subramanyam in a road traffic accident dated 02.07.2018.
2.

The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, on 02.07.2018 at about 8.20 p.m., the deceased was traveling as a cleaner in DCM Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP03TE7095, near Vaviletipasu cross road,
Prakasham, Andhra Pradesh, the said lorry driver drove the lorry in rash and negligent manner and hit the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.AP16BY2069 and also the lorry fell turtle, as a result both the lorry driver and cleaner (deceased) died on the spot.

Thereafter, postmortem was conducted in Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences Hospital and handed over the body to them and they performed funeral SCCH24 obsequious ceremonies by spending more than Rs.2,00,000/.
3.

sentences.text: The petitioners further stated that, at the time of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as a mason and cleaner and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.

Due to the sudden and untimely death of the deceased, they have lost all their income and deceased was only bread earner in their family and they depending on him for their food, cloth and shelter and put them into great agony, pain, frustration and deep mental stress.
The Jarugumalli Police have registered crime against the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.AP 03TE7095 in CR No.58/2018 under Section 279, 338 and 304(A) of the IPC.
Therefore, the Respondents being the insurer and the owner offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to them.

sentences.text: In response to service of notice issued by this court/Tribunal, the Respondent No.1 have appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent No.2 did not appear and hence placed exparte.

5. The Respondent No.1 insurance company in the written statement has denied all the allegations made by the petitioner as false, admitted admitted issuance of policy but their liability is subject to terms and conditions and submitted that there is non compliance of Section 134(c) and Section 158(6) of M.V. Act and the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties as owner and insurer of the two wheeler which involved in the accident are not made as parties and insured vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident.

Further submitted that the owner of the DCM lorry knowing fully well that the vehicle had no FC and the driver did not possess valid and SCCH24 effective DL willfully entrusted the vehicle to the said driver and thereby committed the breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Banda Subramanya had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 02.07.2018 at about 8.20 p.m., near Vaviletipadu cross road, Prakasham, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg.No.AP03TE7095 by its driver as alleged ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4. What order or award ?
SCCH24 7.

Banda Saraswathi wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.15 which evidence is got discarded vide order dated 20.08.2022 and the very same petitioner No.1 is examined as PW1 and Exs.P1 to 15 marked on 10.12.2020 are adopted to the PW.1.
On the other side, the Respondent No.1 did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

9. My findings to the above issues are as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4: As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 is the minor son, Petitioner Nos.3 and 4 are the parents of deceased - Banda Subramanyam.
In this regard, the Petitioners have examined wife of the deceased by name Smt.Banda Saraswathi as PW.1.
The PW.1 has specifically deposed this relationship in her chiefexamination.

Apart SCCH24 from that, to prove the relationship the Petitioners have also produced notarized copies of Aadhar Cards of the petitioner Nos.1 to 4 and the deceased as per Exs.P.10 to P.14 and also produced the death certificate of the deceased at Ex.P.17.
There is no contrary to these documents from the respondent.
In the Aadhaar card of the Petitioner No.1, her husband's name is mentioned as Banda Subhramanyam.

In the Aadhaar card of the Petitioner No.2 his father's name is mentioned as B.Subhramanyam and in the Aadhar card of the Petitioner No.3 his father's name is mentioned as B.Venkatappa, in the Aadhar card of the Petitioner No.4 her husband's name is mentioned as B.Chinnappa who is none other than the Petitioner No.3 and in the Aadhar card of the deceased Banda Subhramanyam, his father's name is mentioned as B.Chinnappa who is the petitioner No.3.
Further, these documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not SCCH24 been seriously disputed by the Respondents.
The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are the wife, minor son and parents of the deceased Banda Subhramanyam.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:

The Petitioners, in order to prove that the accident was occurred due to the actionable negligence on part of the driver of the offending vehicle have examined the Petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and produced 9 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.9.

The PW.1 has specifically stated in his SCCH24 evidence that the on 02.07.2018 at about 8.20 p.m., near Vavilelipadu cross road,
Prakasham, Andhrapradesh, when her husband was travelling as a cleaner in DCM lorry bearing Reg.No.AP03TE7095 the said lorry driver drove the lorry in rash and negligent manner and hit the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.AP16BY2069 and also the lorry fell turtle and due to this impact, her husband fell down sustained severe blood stained injuries all over the body and he died on spot.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 have denied that the vehicle bearing No.AP03 TE7095 was involved in the alleged accident.
But the Respondent No.1 have not lead any evidence.
In the crossexamination of the PW.1 nothing worth is elicited.

sentences.text: Perusal of police documents makes it clear that the deceased of this case was cleaner in lorry bearing No:AP03TE7095 and when the driver of the lorry driven SCCH24 it in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of one Valivarthi Appalarju and who also died alongwith the driver and cleaner of the said lorry.
To disprove the contents of the police documents and the case of the petitioners with regard to alleged manner of accident the respondent No.1 have not lead any contrary evidence.

The petitioners apart from the oral evidence has produced the documents such as FIR in Cr.No.58/2018 of Jarugumalli Police Station, complaint, English translation copy of complaint, PM report, Inquest panchanama, English translation copy of Inquest panchanama, list of witnesses in Cr.No.58/18, translation copy of list of witness, list of the blood relatives and witnesses in Cr.No.58/2018, translation copy of it, Accident report in Cr.No.58/18,
Spot sketch, translation copy of spot sketch and chargesheet along with memo of evidence as per Exs.P.1 to P.9, Ex.P.2(a), 4(a), 5(a), 6(a) and 8(a).

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of SCCH24 PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P9 and appreciating them which are public documents having presumptive value under law, in absence of contrary evidence this Tribunal is of the opinion that the driver of the offending vehicle driven it with rash or negligent manner and caused accident in which the deceased sustained severe injuries and died at spot as alleged by the claimant.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:

The PW.1 has specifically deposed before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and their loving person and further stated that deceased Banda Subramanyam was working as a mason and cleaner and earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
This court while considering the Issue No.2 has already come to the SCCH 24 conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Under such circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation.
Monthly income 14.
According to the Petitioners the deceased was working as a mason and cleaner and earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
In this regard they have not examined any witness and no documents like Bank Account statement etc., are produced to prove the income of the deceased.
In the absence of specific documents for proof of income, the version of the Petitioners that the deceased was earning Rs15,000/ per month is not acceptable.

The counsel for the petitioners submits that though the accident took place in Andhra Pradesh the notional income approved by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority is to be considered as the Hon'ble H.C. also considered the said notional SCCH 24 income in MFA No.4623/2020(MV) in which also it was a case of accident in Andhra Pradesh.

The counsel for the respondent No.1 contended that as the accident took place in Andhra Pradesh and hence notional income approved by KSLSA cannot be applied in this case and further contended that the said aspect observed in the decision relied by him (which is referred above),
wherein the Hon'ble court held that the accident occurred outside Karnataka STate and petitioners are residents of Andhra Pradesh and as per the Central Government Notification, minimum wages in Andhra Pradesh is lesser than that of the Karnataka STate and based on the minimum wages prevailing in Karnataka State, the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has issued Guidelines with reference to taking notional income on year wise basis. Admittedly the accident occurred in Andhra Pradesh and petitioners are residents of said State.

The decision relied upon by the counsel Banda Saraswathi vs Cholamandalam Ms General on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160231489/
5 for the petitioners which is referred above the SCCH24 Hon'ble H.C. considered the notional income guidelines of KSLSA only even though the accident occurred in Andhra Pradesh.

entities.text: Banda Saraswathi vs Cholamandalam Ms General
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With due respect to the decision relied upon by the counsel for the respondent No.1 this Tribunal is of the view that it has no binding force on this Tribunal and hence not applicable.
Moreover, the KSLSA prepared the notional income chart applicable to all districts coming under the respective Hon'ble High Courts of Karnataka, only and specifically for the districts.

Further, notional income is notional income and as the present case is filed before this Tribunal which comes under the Hon'ble H.C. of Karnataka at Bengaluru and therefore, the said chart of notional income is to be considered as applicable to this Tribunal also.
Therefore, in absence of specific proof of evidence and as per the discussion made above, this court has to consider the income of the deceased notionally for calculating the compensation.
At the time of accident the deceased was a young person aged about 25 years as SCCH24 could be make out from Ex.P.14/Aadhar card of the deceased.
He was hale and healthy before accident.
The accident took place in the year 2018.

Therefore, having regard to the age of the deceased and relying the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in the case of Sumangala & Others and Ramanagouda &Anr., in MFA No:202534/2019(MVC) the notified notional income chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is considered for fixing the notional income and accordingly the monthly notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.12,500/ per month.

Age of the deceased:
15.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced Notarized copy of Aadhar card of the deceased as per Ex.P.14.
The accident was occurred on 02.07.2018.

Therefore,
the age of the deceased is considered 25 years.

SCCH24  i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:
As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation,
appropriate multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 18.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, as per the discussion made above the deceased has wife, minor daughter and parents.
As the petitioner No.3 is a old aged person and hence he also needs to be considered as Dependant and hence the petitioners 1 to 4 all are considered as depending on the income of the deceased.
As per the decision in Sarala Verma's case if the total dependents are 4 to 6 in numbers then 1/4th needs to be deducted in the total income of the deceased as living and personal expenses.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others, even in case of the self employed and fixed salary also the Petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Vs Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As mentioned SCCH24 above, in the present case since the deceased is in the age group of below 40 years, 40%
future prospects have to be added to his monthly income.

If 40% income is added to his monthly income, it comes around Rs.17,500/ (Rs.12,500/ + Rs.5,000/) and if 1/4th of his income is deducted towards his living and personal expenses, then the balance comes to Rs.13,125/
(Rs.17,500/  Rs.4,375/).

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.28,35,000/

6 (Rs.13,125/ X 12 X 18 = Rs.28,35,000/).
ii) TRANSPORTATION, MEDICAL AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:

entities.text: Banda Saraswathi vs Cholamandalam Ms General
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In so far as the medical, funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioners have pleaded that they have spent Rs.2,00,000/ amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
In this regard they have not produced any documents to show the expenses.

However, looking into the facts and SCCH24 circumstances of the case, it would be appropriate to award compensation of Rs.17,000/
towards funeral and transportation expenses.
iii) LOSS TO THE ESTATE:

As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.12,500/
per month.
Out of this, he was getting 1/4th of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favour of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled for a sum of Rs.17,000/ under the head of loss to the estate.
iv) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased.
She has lost her husband at the age of 22 years and she has to live remaining part of her life without him.

Therefore,
she is entitled for consortium.
In Magma General Insurance SCCH24 company Limited the Hon'ble Apex court has considered the compensation under head of loss of consortium.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance SCCH24 company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex court in three judge Bench in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @
Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410, had reaffirmed the view of the two judge Bench in Magma General Insurance company Ltd.

entities.text:
United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @
Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Paragraph 53 to 65, dealt with three conventional heads and discussed about "Consortium" to be a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium, as well as filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
Filial Consortium - A child's society, affection and companionship given to a parent.
Therefore, the claimants are also entitled for compensation under the head of consortium.

As such,
the Petitioners are entitled a sum of Rs.1,60,000/ (Rs.40,000/ each) under this head.
As SCCH 24 such, in total the compensation comes to Rs.30,29,000/.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.30,29,000/ .

LIABILITY:
16.
As discussed above the Respondent No.1  insurer have not proved their defence.
There is no dispute with regard to existence of policy as on the date of accident.
Therefore the respondents 1 and 2 being insurer and RC owner are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, as the policy is existed and hence the respondent No.1 is to indemnify the respondent No.2 insured and directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

The counsel for the respondent No.1 contended that the petitioners have amended the petition recently and hence the interest be waived off from the date of petition till the date of amendment as they filed the written statement earlier only to the earlier petition.

No SCCH24 doubt the petitioners have amended the petition recently when the application came to be allowed the application filed for amendment but as per settled law the amendment relates back to the date of petition itself and moreover the amendment was carried based on the contents of the police documents and not otherwise and no new facts are introduced Banda Saraswathi vs Cholamandalam Ms General on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160231489/
7

entities.text: Banda Saraswathi vs Cholamandalam Ms General

sentences.text: and hence the said contention of the respondent No.1 cannot be considered as petitioners cannot be deprived of their right due to some clerical mistake crept in the petition which alter amended.

The Petitioners have claimed an amount of Rs.40,00,000/, but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.30,29,000/ alongwith interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Therefore the Petition is allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 is partly in the Affirmative.
SCCH24 17. Issue No.4:

In view of findings from the above discussions, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.30,29,000/(Rupees Thirty Lakhs and Twenty Nine Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the Respondent SCCH24 No.1 insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, 10% each shall be deposited in the names of the Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 in any N/S bank for a period of 3 years and till petitioner No.2 attains the age of majority respectively with a liberty to withdraw the interest and in the remaining compensation, 15% and 10% shall be released in the name of the Petitioners 3 and 4 respectively and remaining entire compensation shall be released in the name of petitioner No.1 by way of epayment with proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules

. 
SCCH24
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are the wife, minor son and parents of the deceased Banda Subhramanyam.
Perusal of police documents makes it clear that the deceased of this case was cleaner in lorry bearing No:AP03TE7095 and when the driver of the lorry driven SCCH24 it in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of one Valivarthi Appalarju and who also died alongwith the driver and cleaner of the said lorry.
To disprove the contents of the police documents and the case of the petitioners with regard to alleged manner of accident the respondent No.1 have not lead any contrary evidence.
Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of SCCH24 PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P9 and appreciating them which are public documents having presumptive value under law, in absence of contrary evidence this Tribunal is of the opinion that the driver of the offending vehicle driven it with rash or negligent manner and caused accident in which the deceased sustained severe injuries and died at spot as alleged by the claimant.
In the absence of specific documents for proof of income, the version of the Petitioners that the deceased was earning Rs15,000/ per month is not acceptable.
Therefore, in absence of specific proof of evidence and as per the discussion made above, this court has to consider the income of the deceased notionally for calculating the compensation.
At the time of accident the deceased was a young person aged about 25 years as SCCH24 could be make out from Ex.P.14/Aadhar card of the deceased.
He was hale and healthy before accident.
The accident took place in the year 2018.
Therefore, having regard to the age of the deceased and relying the decision of Hon'ble H.C. in the case of Sumangala & Others and Ramanagouda &Anr., in MFA No:202534/2019(MVC) the notified notional income chart of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is considered for fixing the notional income and accordingly the monthly notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.12,500/ per month.
SCCH24  i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:
As per principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation,
appropriate multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 18.
As the petitioner No.3 is a old aged person and hence he also needs to be considered as Dependant and hence the petitioners 1 to 4 all are considered as depending on the income of the deceased.
As per the decision in Sarala Verma's case if the total dependents are 4 to 6 in numbers then 1/4th needs to be deducted in the total income of the deceased as living and personal expenses.
The Hon'ble Apex court in three judge Bench in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @
Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410, had reaffirmed the view of the two judge Bench in Magma General Insurance company Ltd.
Therefore, the claimants are also entitled for compensation under the head of consortium.
However, as the policy is existed and hence the respondent No.1 is to indemnify the respondent No.2 insured and directed to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
